reviews.title: Genuinely awful
reviews.text:
As if shoving ads for AI in my face every 2 minutes wasn’t insult enough, I’ve gone to the trouble of painstakingly creating my Japanese kanji flashcards only for the spaced repetition program to allow me to view a mere FOUR cards a day, even though I set it to 500 cards.

Once I’ve met my generous 4 card allowance, a 24 hour timer starts up which I have no option to dismiss or disable. SRSS apps should NEVER force a timer on you for when you are allowed to study; that is up to ME to decide. Don’t waste your time with this app.

reviews.title: Poor Customer Service
reviews.text:
WARNING: THINK TWICE BEFORE SUBSCRIBING TO KNOWT.

I was charged $119 on September 10 for a subscription I never intended to renew. I’m only 14 years old, and I genuinely did not mean to spend that much money on a subscription I no longer wanted. I explained my situation and asked for a refund, but they still refused to return my money.

I’m extremely disappointed that even after explaining that I’m a student who never intended to make this purchase, my request was denied. This experience has completely damaged my trust in Knowt.

BE CAREFUL BEFORE SUBSCRIBING. Make sure you understand the renewal terms, because forgetting to cancel could cost you $119. I regret subscribing and would warn other students to think twice before paying for this service.

reviews.title: Scam Disguised as a Free Trial
reviews.text:
Knowt is one of the most deceptive apps I’ve ever encountered on the App Store. It lures users in with a so-called “free trial,” but instead of honoring that, it immediately charged $102 from my bank account. There was no clear warning, no transparent confirmation, and no honest disclosure of what I was actually agreeing to. This is not how a legitimate subscription works — it’s how users get scammed.

To make matters worse, after taking that money, Knowt did not even provide a full one-year subscription, which is what a charge of this size would reasonably imply. So not only was the charge deceptive, but the service itself was incomplete and misrepresented. That is false advertising and failure to deliver what was paid for.

This app relies on intentionally confusing wording, dark-pattern design, and vague trial language to trap users into expensive subscriptions they never knowingly agreed to. It feels predatory, especially considering this app targets students. Nothing about this experience was honest, transparent, or ethical.

I am disputing the charge, reporting this app to Apple, and warning others to stay far away. If you value your money, do not download Knowt, do not start the “free trial,” and do not trust this company’s billing practices. Apps like this give the App Store a bad name and should not be allowed on the platform.
